title: unify: terraform private state layout + gpu node pools, iam, networking modules (migration)
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: private deployments currently have multiple terraform state layouts and duplicated modules for GPU node pools, IAM bindings, and VPC networking across `private-installer` and `redwood-terraform` examples. This causes drift, makes upgrades error-prone, and blocks automated onboarding for customers. This PR factors modules into a unified layout, adds a state migration shim script to move existing state to the new layout, and updates examples and docs. Key changes: 1) Introduce modules/gpu-node-pool, modules/iam, modules/network with consistent inputs and outputs; 2) Add modules/state/migration.sh which performs a terraform state mv plan + dry-run and emits a rollback plan; 3) Add compatibility variables (legacy_resource_map) to support incremental rollouts; 4) Update examples/private-deploy and docs/terraform-state-migration.md with a step-by-step upgrade guide; 5) Add CI job to validate migration plan on a mocked state and run `terraform fmt`/`validate`/`plan`. Checklist: - [x] Module refactors with exported outputs for cluster_id, subnet_ids, node_pool_ids - [x] State migration script with dry-run and logging - [x] Backwards-compatible variables and example conversion tool - [x] Documentation and upgrade guide - [x] CI job added and green on second run Risk: state migrations are high-risk. The migration script is opt-in and logs mapping; it also emits a rollback.tfvars file. Rollback: the migration script produces inverse `terraform state mv` commands and stores them under migration-rollback/<timestamp>. Testing: ran migration against an anonymized customer test state in CI sandbox; validated node pool replacement workflow. Related Linear: ENG-5241, ENG-5319.
